the question comes down to who wants these bridges burnt.

Who, exactly, is issuing these ultimatums that force you to choose?

Because if there is anything I have learned, it is this:

Love is not a weapon.
Love is not a tool.
Love is not a currency.

If someone is doing something that causes you great pain, but how much they love you 'makes it okay', that is not love.
If someone has done nice things to you and simply expects your love in return as a quid pro quo, that is not love.
If you must comply to another's will in order to receive their love, that is not love.

But if none of these things are happening with specific regard to the individual you are calling your significant other,
IF it is a family or a community that is treating love like a "payment" that shall be withheld from you because you care about an individual of whom they disapprove,
IF it is others who are issuing ultimatums and your romantic partner only wishes to support you and empower you and NOT restrict you,
then you are right to leave your home behind, even if it hurts.

It's hard to tell. It's really hard to tell who is actually making the unreasonable demands. Just remember to ask yourself, with whom do you feel less entrapped, less restricted, less controlled? Go with them.

Edit: The reason I have so many ifs is because I've seen it go both ways.

I've seen a friend abducted by someone selfish and cruel, made to cut ties with the friends, family, and community they once adored being a part of, all in the name of their so-called "love". It was a disaster. She was never the same. It destroyed the beautiful, vibrant, energetic being we once knew and left a broken, hollow, used up shell in her place. She's still out there, alone, unsupported but for "him", unable to reach out, unable to speak for herself. The police can't make it stop because she's too afraid to press charges. Too afraid that he's right: "You're nothing without me." "I've done everything for you." "You can't survive on your own." "You'd be dead without me."

I've also seen, luckily, several inversions to that scenario. Where someone dear to me was in an abusive, toxic household in a repressive community that doggedly strove to discourage them or tie them down. Working together, our circle of friends was able to extract them from these horrible places, empower them to sever the bonds of manipulation their captors once held, and now they live with agency over their own free will, able to make their own decisions with the knowledge that neither I nor any of the others who care about them will ever reject them for how they feel or what they believe.

It's actually startling how similar these two stories can seem depending on your perspective.

But I implore you:

Do not ever simply ALLOW someone to punish you for having different opinions or beliefs. The moment that happens, start planning an escape. Reach out to whoever might hear you. Friendly strangers. Coworkers. Encouraging voices from the 'net.
